original_question: If a permutation σ occurs precisely once in a permutation π and the Möbius function of the interval [σ, π] is μ(σ, π) = ±1, determine whether the order complex Δ(σ, π) must be homotopy equivalent to a sphere.
target_in_paper: Section 5.2, the third item in the list of topology questions reproduced from [19, Question 31]: whether single-occurrence intervals with Möbius value ±1 have spherical order complex.
correct_elements: The draft already captures the exact core of the paper-faithful question: the hypotheses that σ occurs precisely once in π and that μ(σ, π)=±1, together with the topological conclusion asking whether Δ(σ, π) is homotopy equivalent to a sphere.
missing_details: The ambient object is the permutation pattern poset P of all finite permutations ordered by classical pattern containment.
Δ(σ, π) should be defined explicitly as the order complex of the open interval (σ, π), i.e. of the poset obtained from [σ, π] by removing σ and π.
"σ occurs precisely once in π" means exactly one classical occurrence of σ as a pattern in π.
μ(σ, π) is the Möbius function of the interval [σ, π] in the poset P.
The paper presents this as an open topological question about intervals in P, not as a proved theorem or as part of a broader classification problem.
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; the missing context is purely combinatorial and topological.
refined_question: In the permutation pattern poset P of all finite permutations ordered by classical pattern containment, let [σ, π] be an interval and let Δ(σ, π) denote the order complex of the open interval (σ, π), that is, of [σ, π] with σ and π removed. If σ occurs exactly once as a classical pattern in π and μ(σ, π)=±1, is Δ(σ, π) necessarily homotopy equivalent to a sphere?
justification: The draft clearly targets the topological open problem in §5.2, not the other conjectural material elsewhere in the survey. The refined version stays as close as possible to the paper’s actual intent by preserving the exact hypotheses and conclusion while adding only the notation and ambient-poset definitions needed to make the question stand alone. I did not broaden it to the neighboring questions about wedges of spheres, purity, or shellability. The nearby context also explains why the condition μ(σ, π)=±1 is topologically suggestive: the Möbius function equals the reduced Euler characteristic of the order complex, and the survey notes that no counterexamples were known to this question, even without the single-occurrence assumption.
